rubric.role_summary: Computational protein design scientist working at the interface of generative AI and synthetic biology, leading protein design campaigns and connecting model development with experimental validation.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Computational protein design scientist working at the interface of generative AI and synthetic biology, leading protein design campaigns and connecting model development with experimental validation.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- Experience in computational protein design.
- Hands-on experience with AI generative modeling.
- PhD or equivalent industry experience in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, biochemistry, structural biology, physics, biophysics, bio/chem engineering, or a related field.
- Research experience in protein biochemistry using computational expertise.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Experience applying generative AI or other machine learning models in synthetic biology.
- Experience with homology-based and structural bioinformatics and answering scientific questions using very large databases.
- Startup experience helping a young biotech grow.
- Track record of running end-to-end protein design campaigns, using novel computational tools and biochemistry or structural biology knowledge to design proteins for functional requirements and synthetic biology applications.
- AI generative modeling experience, including both model training and large-scale inference.
- Experience collaborating with experimental wet-lab teams to achieve protein design objectives.
- Track record of delivering commercial and/or academic research projects, demonstrated through publications, patents, commercially impactful outcomes, and/or other scientific-community contributions.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Location: Greater London area. Hybrid work is based in this area, and candidates must currently be located in it. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them.
